claude.sample_unit: older adults in external validation cohort (660,417 in development)

links.outcome: Calibration before vs after local recalibration in external validation cohort
links.effect: Recalibration corrected over-prediction: pooled calibration slope 0.964 (95% CI 0.908 to 1.020), CITL 0.064 (95% CI -0.027 to 0.154), vs CITL -0.874 before; discrimination unchanged.
links.quote: Recalibration did not affect the discrimination performance or variability in calibration across practices (Supplementary Figures S3.12/S3.14), but corrected average over-prediction on apparent validation, giving a pooled calibration slope of 0.964 (95% CI: 0.908 to 1.020) and pooled CITL of 0.064 (95% CI: −0.027 to 0.154).

links.outcome: Calibration of model applied to new population (external validation)
links.effect: Model over-predicted risk in Bradford: pooled CITL -0.874 (95% CI -0.964 to -0.783), O/E 0.43 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.48); no better than treat-none at 10-25% thresholds.
links.quote: Calibration curves ( Figure 1 ) show that the eFalls model over-predicted fall/fracture risk in the Connect Bradford population, with predicted risks exceeding observed risks across the full range of possible predicted values.

links.outcome: Variation in calibration and net benefit across general practices
links.effect: Extent of over-prediction highly variable across GP practices; net benefit highly variable and did not stabilise with recalibration; c-statistic consistently above 0.6 in all practices.
links.quote: As with calibration performance, net benefit was highly variable across GP practices, which did not stabilise with recalibration (Supplementary Figure S3.13).

links.outcome: Model discrimination and calibration across clinical and deprivation subgroups
links.effect: Fairly consistent across sex and deprivation; discrimination lower in severe frailty (c-statistic 0.643); over-prediction most evident in underweight and severely frail; poor performance in those missing WIMD.
links.quote: Model performance was fairly consistent across sexes and deprivation subgroups, while over-prediction of falls risk was most evident in those who were underweight and those who had severe frailty.

links.outcome: Miscalibration from differences between development and validation populations
links.effect: Fall incidence 4.9% in development vs 2.9% in validation, differing coding systems; model over-predicted risk in the external population (O/E 0.43).
links.quote: This overestimation of risk was likely due to the higher incidence of falls in the development (4.9%) compared to the external validation cohorts (2.9%).

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration on internal vs external validation data
links.effect: C-statistic 0.72 on internal-external cross-validation vs 0.82 external; external validation revealed miscalibration (CITL -0.87) that internal validation did not show.
links.quote: While the eFalls model was well calibrated on internal and internal–external cross-validation (in Welsh national-level data in SAIL), on external validation in Connected Bradford, although there was evidence for excellent discrimination, fall/fracture risk was slightly overestimated on average.

links.outcome: Net benefit at clinician-specified risk thresholds (10-25%) on external validation
links.effect: Model was no better than treat-none in the prespecified 10-25% range before recalibration; after recalibration superior for thresholds up to 18%.
links.quote: Decision curves show that the eFalls model had clinical utility at lower threshold probabilities on external validation, but was no better than the treat-none alternative in the pre-specified range of 10–25%.

links.outcome: external calibration and discrimination
links.effect: External c-statistic 0.82 (95% CI: 0.80 to 0.83); calibration-in-the-large, -0.87 (95% CI: -0.96 to -0.78).
links.quote: Calibration was variable across practices, with some over-prediction in the validation population (calibration-in-the-large, -0.87; 95% CI: -0.96 to -0.78).

links.outcome: dataset shift and calibration
links.effect: Fall/fracture incidence 4.9% in development versus 2.9% in external cohorts; authors attributed overestimation to this difference.
links.quote: This overestimation of risk was likely due to the higher incidence of falls in the development (4.9%) compared to the external validation cohorts (2.9%).

links.outcome: recalibration calibration
links.effect: Corrected average over-prediction on apparent validation: calibration slope 0.964 (95% CI: 0.908 to 1.020); CITL 0.064 (95% CI: −0.027 to 0.154).
links.quote: Recalibration did not affect the discrimination performance or variability in calibration across practices (Supplementary Figures S3.12/S3.14), but corrected average over-prediction on apparent validation, giving a pooled calibration slope of 0.964 (95% CI: 0.908 to 1.020) and pooled CITL of 0.064 (95% CI: −0.027 to 0.154).

links.outcome: practice-level performance
links.effect: Across external practices, CITL 95% prediction interval −1.375 to −0.372; c-statistic prediction interval 0.715 to 0.886.
links.quote: The extent of over-prediction was highly variable across GP practices (see Figures 3 and S3.12), but was seen consistently across subgroups by IMD, frailty, sex and BMI (Supplementary Figures S3.15–S3.18).

links.outcome: frailty subgroup discrimination
links.effect: Severely frail subgroup c-statistic 0.643 (95% CI: 0.638 to 0.646), lower than overall external 0.816.
links.quote: When assessed across frailty groups, discrimination was notably lower in the severely frail subgroup, with a c-statistic of 0.643 (95% CI: 0.638 to 0.646), most likely due to the narrower case-mix distribution.

links.outcome: new-setting miscalibration
links.effect: External validation showed miscalibration: O/E 0.432 overall and pooled across practices O/E 0.431 (95% CI: 0.388 to 0.479).
links.quote: Due to differences in systems and coding ontologies across the model development and validation datasets, the eFalls model showed some miscalibration on external validation.

links.outcome: calibration and net benefit after local recalibration
links.effect: Recalibration corrected over-prediction (pooled calibration slope 0.964, CITL 0.064 vs uncalibrated 1.203, -0.874) and improved net benefit, making it superior for threshold probabilities up to 18%.
links.quote: Recalibration did not affect the discrimination performance or variability in calibration across practices (Supplementary Figures S3.12/S3.14), but corrected average over-prediction on apparent validation, giving a pooled calibration slope of 0.964 (95% CI: 0.908 to 1.020) and pooled CITL of 0.064 (95% CI: −0.027 to 0.154).

screen.reason: Pure model development and retrospective external validation study without evaluation of deployment, workflow, safety guardrails, or human use.
